styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Royal palaces, cafés and the Egyptian Museum.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Aperitivo, gianduja chocolate and Piedmontese wine.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Roman streets, Savoy palaces and Italy's first capital.

stays.why: Walk to Piazza Castello, the Egyptian Museum and the cafés. Best base for a first visit.
Next to the main station and Metro Linea 1. Easy arrival and good value hotels.
High-speed train hub with metro links. Quieter streets, a short walk or ride to the centre.
The old Fiat factory with its rooftop track, plus a mall and art. Cheaper, but you ride the metro to the centre.

food: Start the day with a bicerin, a hot coffee-chocolate drink, at a historic café in the centre.
Aperitivo is a Turin ritual: one drink, then a buffet of snacks, usually €8–12.
Try Piedmontese dishes: agnolotti pasta, vitello tonnato and tajarin. Book dinner ahead on weekends.
Buy gianduja chocolate and gianduiotti at old-school chocolate shops. Prices vary; check the counter.
Look for the fixed-price lunch menus (menù del giorno) at trattorias, often €12–18.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a trip to the Reggia di Venaria, a Savoy palace outside town. Check transport and opening hours on the day.
Take the train to Asti or Alba for wine country. Timetables and prices vary; check on the day.
Ride the historic tram or funicular up to Superga for city views. Check the schedule before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Egyptian Museum, the royal palaces and a proper aperitivo; add a night for a palace or wine-country day trip.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 8°C and lows below freezing. Pack a warm coat.
February: still cold, highs around 10°C. Fewer crowds at museums.
March: milder at 14°C, some rain. Good for walking the centre.
April: pleasant at 18°C but rainier, with about 10 wet days.
May: warm at 21°C and the wettest month, around 16 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
June: warm and sunny, highs near 27°C. Good outdoor evenings.
July: hot, highs around 30°C. Sightsee early and rest at midday.
August: hot like July, around 29°C. Many locals are away; some shops close.
September: warm at 24°C and comfortable. A strong month to visit.
October: mild at 18°C with some rain. Good for food and wine trips.
November: cooler at 12°C with around 9 rain days. Bring layers.
December: cold again, highs near 8°C. Christmas lights and markets in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate with cold winters and warm summers. Rain is spread across the year, heaviest in spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Mild days around 18–24°C. Good for walking and day trips.

items.title: Summer is hot but not extreme
items.text: July and August reach about 30°C. Go to museums at midday and walk in the evening.

items.title: Winter is cold
items.text: December to February see highs near 8–10°C and lows at or below freezing. Bring a warm coat.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: May is wettest with about 16 rain days. Keep a small umbrella handy in spring and autumn.

items.title: Po valley haze
items.text: Winter days can be grey and foggy. Plan indoor sights as backup.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Add a hat and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Walk in the centre; use Metro Linea 1 and trams for longer hops.

modes.text: Linea 1 runs driverless trains from Bengasi to Fermi, linking Porta Nuova and Porta Susa.
Buses and trams run 06:00–00:30. Buy tickets before boarding from tobacconists or machines. A standard 'City + Suburban 100' ticket costs €2 and is valid for 100 minutes.
Taxis are available but ride apps like Uber are limited. Use FreeNow or local apps.
Driving in the centre is not recommended due to restricted streets and trams.
Walking is ideal in the centre. Bike sharing is available via Lime and RideMovi.
